This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual  /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. This is an application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the Petitioner for bail in connection with Soro P.S.Case No.385 of 2023 corresponding to C.T.Case No.801 of 2023 pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Soro for alleged commission of offence under Sections 447, 294, 379, 324, 307, 506, 323/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that earlier this matter was not before any other Bench of this Court.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 23.03.2024.
It is also contended by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that in the meantime the investigation has been concluded and Charge Sheet has been submitted.
He further contended that the injured has sustained two injuries out of which one is grievous in nature.
So far the fracture injury is concerned, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Malaya Biswal@Sukuta vs State Of Odisha .....

same is on the face of the injured and he has been discharged after getting preliminary treatment.
Now the injured is hale and hearty.

Further referring to the antecedent of the Petitioner, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that although it has been shown that the Petitioner is having four criminal antecedents, against the two cases the Petitioner has not been charge sheeted and in other two cases in one case 498 of the Indian Penal Code and the other one is 376, 294, 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
He further contended that since the Petitioner belongs to the locality there is no chance of his absconding.
On such ground learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner be released on bail on any terms and conditions.
5. Learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State on the other hand objected to the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the injury was grievous in nature.
He also contended that the injured has sustained injury on vital part of his body.
It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the State that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail there is every possibility of his involvement in similar nature of offence.
On such ground, learned counsel for the State submitted that the prayer for bail of the Petitioner be rejected.

6. Having heard learned counsels for the respective parties as well as on careful examination of the materials on record and considering the seriousness of the allegations in the F.I.R. as well as the period of custodial detention and the fact that the injured has already discharged in the meantime,
Charge Sheet has been filed, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the Petitioner and it is directed that let the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter.

Release of the Petitioner shall be subject to such terms and conditions as would be fixed by the learned court in seisin over the matter Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
7.
The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge RKS Location: High Court of Orissa Malaya Biswal@Sukuta vs State Of Odisha .....
